# Global development guidelines for the LangChain monorepo

This document provides context to understand the LangChain Python project and assist with development.

<corridor>

## Corridor security analysis

When Corridor's `analyzePlan` tool is available, create a plan and use the tool to analyze it before generating or modifying code. Apply the resulting security guidance before writing code.

</corridor>

## Project architecture and context

### Monorepo structure

This is a Python monorepo with multiple independently versioned packages that use `uv`.

```txt
langchain/
├── libs/
│   ├── core/             # `langchain-core` primitives and base abstractions
│   ├── langchain/        # `langchain-classic` (legacy, no new features)
│   ├── langchain_v1/     # Actively maintained `langchain` package
│   ├── partners/         # Third-party integrations
│   │   ├── openai/       # OpenAI models and embeddings
│   │   ├── anthropic/    # Anthropic (Claude) integration
│   │   ├── ollama/       # Local model support
│   │   └── ... (other integrations maintained by the LangChain team)
│   ├── text-splitters/   # Document chunking utilities
│   ├── standard-tests/   # Shared test suite for integrations
│   ├── model-profiles/   # Model configuration profiles
├── .github/              # CI/CD workflows and templates
├── .vscode/              # VSCode IDE standard settings and recommended extensions
└── README.md             # Information about LangChain
```

- **Core layer** (`langchain-core`): Base abstractions, interfaces, and protocols. Users should not need to know about this layer directly.
- **Implementation layer** (`langchain`): Concrete implementations and high-level public utilities
- **Integration layer** (`partners/`): Third-party service integrations. Note that this monorepo is not exhaustive of all LangChain integrations; some are maintained in separate repos, such as `langchain-ai/langchain-google` and `langchain-ai/langchain-aws`. Usually these repos are cloned at the same level as this monorepo, so if needed, you can refer to their code directly by navigating to `../langchain-google/` from this monorepo.
- **Testing layer** (`standard-tests/`): Standardized integration tests for partner integrations

### Development tools & commands

- `uv` – Fast Python package installer and resolver (replaces pip/poetry)
- `make` – Task runner for common development commands. Feel free to look at the `Makefile` for available commands and usage patterns.
- `ruff` – Fast Python linter and formatter
- `mypy` – Static type checking
- `pytest` – Testing framework

This monorepo uses `uv` for dependency management. Local development uses editable installs: `[tool.uv.sources]`

Each package in `libs/` has its own `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`.

Before running your tests, set up all packages by running:

```bash
# For all groups
uv sync --all-groups

# or, to install a specific group only:
uv sync --group test
```

```bash
# Run unit tests (no network)
make test

# Run specific test file
uv run --group test pytest tests/unit_tests/test_specific.py
```

```bash
# Lint code
make lint

# Format code
make format

# Type checking
uv run --group lint mypy .
```

#### Environment and dependency management

Use `uv` for all environment and dependency operations in this monorepo. Do not invoke `pip`, `poetry`, or `conda` directly.

- Let `uv` manage the interpreter and virtual environments — `uv sync` and `uv run` operate without manual `source .venv/bin/activate`. Do not create ad-hoc virtual environments outside the package directory.
- Each package targets its own supported Python range via its `pyproject.toml`; do not pin a global Python version. If you need an interpreter explicitly, defer to the package's `requires-python` rather than assuming system Python.
- Install dependencies explicitly through `uv sync` (optionally `--group <name>` / `--all-groups`); never let them install implicitly.
- Don't mix environments within a session, and don't add new dependencies unless strictly required — when you do, justify them (recent releases/commits, adoption).

#### Key config files

- pyproject.toml: Main workspace configuration with dependency groups
- uv.lock: Locked dependencies for reproducible builds
- Makefile: Development tasks

#### PR and commit titles

Follow Conventional Commits. See `.github/workflows/pr_lint.yml` for allowed types and scopes. All titles must include a scope with no exceptions — even for the main `langchain` package.

- Start the text after `type(scope):` with a lowercase letter, unless the first word is a proper noun (e.g. `Azure`, `GitHub`, `OpenAI`) or a named entity (class, function, method, parameter, or variable name).
- Wrap named entities in backticks so they render as code. Proper nouns are left unadorned.
- Keep titles short and descriptive — save detail for the body.

Examples:

```txt
feat(langchain): add new chat completion feature
fix(core): resolve type hinting issue in vector store
chore(anthropic): update infrastructure dependencies
feat(langchain): `ls_agent_type` tag on `create_agent` calls
fix(openai): infer Azure chat profiles from model name
```

#### Branch naming

Branches should be prefixed `<github-username>/<scope>/<short-description>`:

- `<github-username>` — the author's GitHub login (e.g. `mdrxy`).
- `<scope>` — the same scope used in the Conventional Commit title (`core`, `langchain`, partner name, `infra`, `docs`, etc.).
- `<short-description>` — kebab-case, brief, no trailing slash.

Examples:

```txt
mdrxy/anthropic/normalize-tool-call-ids
mdrxy/core/vector-store-type-hints
mdrxy/infra/agents-md-branch
```

#### PR descriptions

The description *is* the summary — do not add a `# Summary` header.

- When the PR closes an issue, lead with the closing keyword on its own line at the very top, followed by a horizontal rule and then the body:

  ```txt
  Closes #123

  ---

  <rest of description>
  ```

  Only `Closes`, `Fixes`, and `Resolves` auto-close the referenced issue on merge. `Related:` or similar labels are informational and do not close anything.

- Explain the *why*: who benefits, what problem they had, and how this solves it. Prefer a simple user story over a long summary.
- Write for readers who may be unfamiliar with this area of the codebase. Avoid insider shorthand and prefer language that is friendly to public viewers — this aids interpretability.
- Do **not** cite line numbers; they go stale as soon as the file changes.
- Rarely include full file paths or filenames. Reference the affected symbol, class, or subsystem by name instead.
- Wrap class, function, method, parameter, and variable names in backticks.
- For net new features or behavior-changing bugfixes, PR descriptions should include a `## Release note` section that states the user-visible change in release-note-ready language.
- Skip dedicated "Test plan" or "Testing" sections in most cases. Mention tests only when coverage is non-obvious, risky, or otherwise notable.
- Call out areas of the change that require careful review.
- Add a brief disclaimer noting AI-agent involvement in the contribution.

## Core development principles

### Maintain stable public interfaces

CRITICAL: Always attempt to preserve function signatures, argument positions, and names for exported/public methods. Do not make breaking changes.
You should warn the developer for any function signature changes, regardless of whether they look breaking or not.

**Before making ANY changes to public APIs:**

- Check if the function/class is exported in `__init__.py`
- Look for existing usage patterns in tests and examples
- Use keyword-only arguments for new parameters: `*, new_param: str = "default"`
- Mark experimental features clearly with docstring warnings (using MkDocs Material admonitions, like `!!! warning`)

Ask: "Would this change break someone's code if they used it last week?"

### Code quality standards

All Python code MUST include type hints and return types.

The agent engineering platform.


LangChain is a framework for building agents and LLM-powered applications. It helps you chain together interoperable components and third-party integrations to simplify AI application development — all while future-proofing decisions as the underlying technology evolves. > [!TIP] > Just getting started? Check out **[Deep Agents](http://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/)** — a higher-level package built on LangChain for agents that have built-in capabilities for common usage patterns such as planning, subagents, file system usage, and more. ## Quickstart ```bash uv add langchain ``` ```python from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model model = init_chat_model("openai:gpt-5.5") result = model.invoke("Hello, world!") ``` If you're looking for more advanced customization or agent orchestration, check out [LangGraph](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph), our framework for building controllable agent workflows. For an equivalent JS/TS library, check out [LangChain.js](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchainjs). > [!TIP] > For developing, debugging, and deploying AI agents and LLM applications, see [LangSmith](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/home). ## LangChain ecosystem While the LangChain framework can be used standalone, it also integrates seamlessly with any LangChain product, giving developers a full suite of tools when building LLM applications. - **[Deep Agents](http://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/)** — Build agents that can plan, use subagents, and leverage file systems for complex tasks - **[LangGraph](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview)** — Build agents that can reliably handle complex tasks with our low-level agent orchestration framework - **[Integrations](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/providers/overview)** — Chat & embedding models, tools & toolkits, and more - **[LangSmith](https://www.langchain.com/langsmith)** — Agent evals, observability, and debugging for LLM apps - **[LangSmith Deployment](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/deployments)** — Deploy and scale agents with a purpose-built platform for long-running, stateful workflows ## Why use LangChain? LangChain helps developers build applications powered by LLMs through a standard interface for models, embeddings, vector stores, and more. - **Real-time data augmentation** — Easily connect LLMs to diverse data sources and external/internal systems, drawing from LangChain's vast library of integrations with model providers, tools, vector stores, retrievers, and more - **Model interoperability** — Swap models in and out as your engineering team experiments to find the best choice for your application's needs. As the industry frontier evolves, adapt quickly — LangChain's abstractions keep you moving without losing momentum - **Rapid prototyping** — Quickly build and iterate on LLM applications with LangChain's modular, component-based architecture. Test different approaches and workflows without rebuilding from scratch, accelerating your development cycle - **Production-ready features** — Deploy reliable applications with built-in support for monitoring, evaluation, and debugging through integrations like LangSmith. Scale with confidence using battle-tested patterns and best practices - **Vibrant community and ecosystem** — Leverage a rich ecosystem of integrations, templates, and community-contributed components. Benefit from continuous improvements and stay up-to-date with the latest AI developments through an active open-source community - **Flexible abstraction layers** — Work at the level of abstraction that suits your needs — from high-level chains for quick starts to low-level components for fine-grained control. LangChain grows with your application's complexity --- ## Resources - [Documentation](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/overview) — conceptual overviews and guides - [LangChain ecosystem overview](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/concepts/products) — how LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents fit together - [API reference](https://reference.langchain.com/python) — complete reference for all public classes, functions, and types - [Discussions](https://forum.langchain.com/c/oss-product-help-lc-and-lg/langchain/14) — community forum for technical questions, ideas, and feedback - [LangChain Academy](https://academy.langchain.com/) — comprehensive, free courses on LangChain libraries and products, made by the LangChain team - [Contributing Guide](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/contributing/overview) — how to contribute and find good first issues - [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/?tab=coc-ov-file) — community guidelines and standards

report.overview: LangChain is a Python monorepo for building LLM-powered agents and applications. The actively maintained `langchain` package (libs/langchain_v1) is a thin orchestration layer over LangGraph: `create_agent()` compiles a tool-calling agent loop into a `CompiledStateGraph`, `init_chat_model()` lazily instantiates provider chat models from a registry, and a middleware system lets users hook every stage of the agent loop. `langchain-core` owns the stable abstractions (Runnable, BaseChatModel, BaseTool, messages, callbacks), `libs/partners/` holds ~17 independently released provider integrations, and `langchain-classic` preserves the legacy chains/agents API without new features.

system_map.summary: A uv-managed Python monorepo of independently versioned packages under libs/. langchain-core defines provider-agnostic abstractions; langchain (langchain_v1) is the user-facing orchestration layer built on LangGraph's StateGraph; langchain-classic is a frozen legacy package; libs/partners/ contains per-provider integrations released individually. There is no server or CLI entrypoint — the 'entrypoints' are library factories (create_agent, init_chat_model, init_embeddings) plus the langchain-profiles CLI. Build is hatchling, tests are pytest, and CI is a set of reusable GitHub Actions workflows.

claims.claim: The repo is a monorepo of independently versioned packages: langchain-core v1.6.4 (libs/core), langchain v1.4.2 (libs/langchain_v1), langchain-classic v1.0.8 (libs/langchain), plus text-splitters, standard-tests (langchain-tests), and model-profiles.

The actively maintained `langchain` package depends only on langchain-core>=1.6.3, langgraph>=1.2.11, and pydantic>=2.7.4; all provider integrations (openai, anthropic, mcp/fastmcp, etc.) are optional extras.

langchain-core is the abstraction layer housing runnables, language_models, messages, tools, callbacks, vectorstores, output_parsers, prompts, tracers, and a _security subpackage; its own deps are langsmith, httpx, tenacity, pydantic, jsonpatch, PyYAML.
The primary public entrypoint is `create_agent`, re-exported from `langchain.agents`, which builds and compiles a LangGraph `StateGraph` into a `CompiledStateGraph`.

`init_chat_model` resolves provider strings like 'openai:gpt-5.5' through the `_BUILTIN_PROVIDERS` registry (~28 entries mapping provider key -> (module_path, class_name, creator_func)) and lazily imports the partner package.

Provider integrations live in libs/partners/ (anthropic, chroma, deepseek, exa, fireworks, groq, huggingface, mistralai, nomic, ollama, openai, openrouter, perplexity, qdrant, xai) each with its own pyproject.toml and uv.lock, and each implementing langchain-core abstractions (e.g. ChatOpenAI in langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py).

langchain-classic is the legacy package: `initialize_agent` is decorated @deprecated since 0.1.0 pointing users to `create_agent`, and its chains/agents tree (AgentExecutor, chains/*) is maintained for backward compatibility only.
All packages build with hatchling and are developed via uv; local cross-package deps use editable `[tool.uv.sources]` path references (e.g. langchain-core -> ../core).
Per-package Makefiles define the dev surface: `make test` (pytest with docker compose postgres+redis services), `make lint` (ruff check + ruff format --diff + mypy), `make format`, `make benchmark`.
CI is organized as reusable workflows: `_test.yml` runs unit tests then re-runs them against computed minimum dependency versions via `.github/scripts/get_min_versions.py`.

Releases are per-package and manually dispatched through `_release.yml` (workflow_call/workflow_dispatch), which resolves a working-directory dropdown value to a PyPI package name (langchain->langchain-classic, langchain_v1->langchain).
The `langchain.mcp` namespace is beta-gated (importing it emits LangChainBetaWarning) and adapts MCP servers via the optional `fastmcp` extra.
openwiki/ contains generated architecture documentation (e.g. architecture.md) that mirrors the three-layer design and is refreshed by the openwiki-update workflow.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface: agent construction (create_agent with middleware, structured output, persistence, interrupts), model/embeddings factories (init_chat_model, init_embeddings), tool authoring (@tool, BaseTool, ToolRuntime injection), a large built-in middleware catalog (HITL, summarization, PII, retries, limits, shell tool, file search, todo lists, tool selection/emulation), MCP server tool adaptation, and message/rate-limiter re-exports. langchain-classic preserves the legacy chains/agents API. langchain-tests ships a conformance suite for partner authors; langchain-profiles ships a CLI for model capability data.

claims.claim: `create_agent(model, tools, system_prompt, middleware, response_format, state_schema, context_schema, checkpointer, store, interrupt_before, interrupt_after, debug, name, cache, transformers)` returns a `CompiledStateGraph` implementing the model->tools loop until no tool_calls remain.

`init_chat_model` supports string specs ('provider:model'), explicit model_provider, configurable_fields producing a deferred `_ConfigurableModel`, and a special 'langsmith' provider that routes ChatOpenAI through the LangSmith gateway (LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY / gateway.smith.langchain.com).
`init_embeddings` provides the same lazy provider-registry pattern for ~10 embeddings providers (azure_openai, bedrock, cohere, google_genai, huggingface, mistralai, ollama, openai, ...).

Tools are authored via the `@tool` decorator (langchain_core.tools.convert) or BaseTool subclasses; langchain.tools re-exports these plus ToolRuntime, InjectedState, and InjectedStore for runtime/state injection into tool functions.

The built-in middleware catalog includes: SummarizationMiddleware, HumanInTheLoopMiddleware, PIIMiddleware, TodoListMiddleware, ModelRetryMiddleware, ModelFallbackMiddleware, ModelCallLimitMiddleware, ToolRetryMiddleware, ToolCallLimitMiddleware, ToolErrorMiddleware, LLMToolSelectorMiddleware, LLMToolEmulator, ContextEditingMiddleware, FilesystemFileSearchMiddleware, ProviderToolSearchMiddleware, and ShellToolMiddleware.

Structured output is configured via `response_format` accepting a raw Pydantic/dataclass/TypedDict/JSON-schema or explicit ToolStrategy/ProviderStrategy/AutoStrategy; AutoStrategy picks provider-native output when `_supports_provider_strategy` says the model supports it.

HumanInTheLoopMiddleware pauses tool calls via langgraph `interrupt()` with ReviewConfig policies allowing approve/edit/reject/respond decisions, and annotates edited calls with an `_EDIT_NOTICE` so the model knows the call was replaced.

ShellToolMiddleware exposes a persistent `shell` tool executing commands under pluggable policies: HostExecutionPolicy (direct subprocess), DockerExecutionPolicy, and CodexSandboxExecutionPolicy, with output redaction via RedactionRule.

PIIMiddleware detects emails/credit cards/IPs/MACs/URLs via `_redaction` helpers and can mutate streaming deltas in flight through `_PIIStreamTransformer` (a 128-char lookback buffer catches patterns straddling token boundaries).

`MCPAdapter` converts FastMCP targets (URL, Path, transport, MCPConfig, in-process server, client/group) into LangChain tools via `list_tools()`, and arms clients so server elicitation requests become LangGraph interrupts answered by humans.
langchain.messages re-exports the canonical message model (AIMessage, ToolMessage, HumanMessage, SystemMessage, content-block types, ToolCall, trim_messages) from langchain-core.

BaseRateLimiter/InMemoryRateLimiter are re-exported from langchain.rate_limiters and are honored by BaseChatModel._generate_with_cache which acquires the limiter before hitting the provider API (but after cache lookup).

langchain-tests (standard-tests) ships reusable conformance suites — unit_tests/chat_models.py, embeddings.py, tools.py and integration_tests/{chat_models,vectorstores,retrievers,indexer,cache,sandboxes}.py — that partner packages subclass to prove compliance.
langchain-model-profiles ships a `langchain-profiles` CLI that generates per-model capability profile data consumed by partners' data/ dirs.

langchain-classic retains the legacy feature surface: AgentExecutor, agent types (react, conversational, structured_chat, tool_calling_agent, openai_functions_*), and the full chains/ tree (retrieval, combine_documents, graph_qa, etc.).

data_flow.summary: Agents are LangGraph state machines: input is a messages list merged into a resolved state schema (middleware schemas + AgentState, base last so caller schema wins conflicts). Each loop iteration builds a ModelRequest carried through the wrap_model_call middleware stack to a bound model; the AIMessage is post-processed for structured output and packed into Command state updates. Tool calls route to ToolNode, whose ToolMessages append via the add_messages reducer. Tool calls go through a wrap_tool_call stack. Streaming is reshaped by TransformerFactory instances registered at compile time. Outside agents, init_chat_model resolves provider strings to lazily imported classes, and BaseChatModel.invoke routes through callbacks, an LLM cache, and a rate limiter before _generate/_stream.

claims.claim: Agent input boundary is `{"messages": [...]}`: `_resolve_schemas` merges each middleware's `state_schema` (in registration order) with the base schema last, producing resolved_state_schema, input_schema, output_schema for the StateGraph.

ModelRequest is the data unit flowing through wrap_model_call middleware: it carries model, messages (excluding system message), system_message, tool_choice, tools, response_format, state, runtime, and model_settings, with an `override()` API (direct attribute assignment is deprecated).

The model node builds a ModelRequest, runs it through the composed `wrap_model_call_handler` (or calls `_execute_model` directly), then `_build_commands` converts the ModelResponse into Command objects updating `messages` and `structured_response` state.

`_get_bound_model` validates middleware-added client-side tools against `tool_node.tools_by_name` (skipped when wrap_tool_call middleware can handle dynamic tools), normalizes raw schemas to AutoStrategy, and picks ProviderStrategy vs ToolStrategy by model capability.

Structured output is marshaled inside `_handle_model_output`: ProviderStrategy parses the AIMessage via `ProviderStrategyBinding.parse`, ToolStrategy intercepts tool_calls matching `structured_output_tools` names and validates args into `structured_response` state.

Tool execution reuses LangGraph's ToolNode — langchain's tools/tool_node.py is a backwards-compat shim re-exporting ToolNode, ToolCallRequest, ToolCallWrapper, InjectedState, InjectedStore, ToolRuntime from langgraph.prebuilt.

Conversation history accumulates in the `messages` channel via langgraph's `add_messages` reducer imported in middleware types; agent state also carries ephemeral routing via JumpTo ('tools'|'model'|'end').

Stream output is post-processed by transformers registered at compile: ToolCallTransformer and SubagentTransformer always run first, then per-middleware `transformers` (e.g. InternalCallTransformer for SummarizationMiddleware's internal calls), then user-supplied factories, deduped.

Tracing flows through LangSmith: middleware wrap hooks are wrapped in `traceable` with `_scrub_inputs` stripping unserializable handler/runtime, per-middleware TracePolicy via `_node_trace_policy`, and the compiled graph gets metadata `ls_integration: langchain_create_agent`.

init_chat_model data flow: provider key lookup in `_BUILTIN_PROVIDERS` -> `_import_module` (importlib with 'pip install <pkg>' hint on failure) -> getattr class -> functools.partial creator; provider inference from model name uses the registry keys.

BaseChatModel.invoke pipelines through callback_manager.on_chat_model_start -> `_generate_with_cache` (llm cache lookup via `dumps(messages)` key, then rate_limiter.acquire) -> either protocol v2 streaming, implicit `_stream` chunk accumulation with on_llm_new_token, or `_generate` -> on_llm_end with LLMResult.

BaseTool.run wraps execution in on_tool_start/on_tool_end callbacks and converts ToolException into tool output content per the tool's `handle_tool_error` flag (bool, str template, or callable) via `_handle_tool_error`.

MCP tool data flow: MCPAdapter builds a FastMCPClient (str targets restricted to http/https), `list_tools` calls client.list_tools(cache_mode) then `as_langchain_tool` per remote tool; elicitation requests surface as langgraph interrupts.

behavior_traces.summary: Key flows traced end-to-end: (1) model initialization via init_chat_model; (2) agent construction via create_agent — middleware classification, schema merge, node/edge wiring, compile; (3) the agent loop — before_agent/before_model hooks, model call through the wrap_model_call stack, tool dispatch, loop-back or exit through after_model/after_agent; (4) single chat-model invocation through cache/rate-limiter/streaming; (5) MCP tool adoption; (6) CI test and release flows.

claims.claim: Import/startup: `import langchain` sets only __version__; `from langchain.agents import create_agent` pulls factory.py which imports langgraph (StateGraph, ToolNode, Command, Send), langsmith.traceable, and init_chat_model; `import langchain.mcp` emits a LangChainBetaWarning.

init_chat_model('openai:gpt-5.5'): parse provider prefix -> `_get_chat_model_creator` (lru_cached) -> `_import_module('langchain_openai')` -> getattr ChatOpenAI -> functools.partial(_call, cls) -> cls(**kwargs); ollama falls back to langchain_community.chat_models for backwards compat.

create_agent construction order: str model -> init_chat_model; system_prompt -> SystemMessage; middleware partitioned by which hooks each subclass overrides (before_agent/before_model/after_model/after_agent/wrap_model_call/wrap_tool_call); sync and async wrap handlers composed via `_chain_model_call_handlers`/`_chain_async_model_call_handlers`.

Graph wiring: nodes added — 'model' (RunnableCallable(model_node, amodel_node)), 'tools' (ToolNode, only if tools exist), and '<middleware_name>.<hook>' RunnableCallables; START->entry_node; conditional edges route tools->loop_entry|exit and model->tools|exit|loop_entry; middleware chains wired via `_add_middleware_edge` with can_jump_to.

Compile step: graph.compile(checkpointer, store, interrupt_before, interrupt_after, debug, name, cache, transformers=[ToolCallTransformer, SubagentTransformer, middleware+user transformers]) then `.with_config({recursion_limit: 9999, metadata: {ls_integration: langchain_create_agent}})`.

Runtime loop order on agent.invoke: START -> first before_agent middleware -> before_model chain -> 'model' -> after_model chain (reverse order) -> conditional edge: tool_calls present -> 'tools' -> back to loop_entry_node (first before_model or 'model'); no tool_calls -> exit_node -> after_agent chain -> END.

Inside the model node (sync path mirrored by amodel_node): ModelRequest assembled -> awrap_model_call_handler(request, _execute_model_async) -> _get_bound_model binds tools and resolves response format -> model.ainvoke(messages) -> _handle_model_output -> ModelResponse -> _build_commands (rejecting Command.goto from wrap_model_call with NotImplementedError).

Structured-output error recovery: StructuredOutputValidationError or MultipleStructuredOutputsError goes through `_handle_structured_output_error`; if retryable, an error ToolMessage (STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_ERROR_TEMPLATE 'Please fix your mistakes.') is appended and the loop continues.

Single chat-model call: BaseChatModel.invoke -> generate -> callback_manager.on_chat_model_start -> _generate_with_cache -> cache.lookup(prompt, llm_string) short-circuits on hit -> rate_limiter.acquire -> protocol-v2 streaming / implicit _stream (on_llm_new_token per chunk) / _generate -> run_manager.on_llm_end(LLMResult).

Tool invocation inside ToolNode delegates to BaseTool.run: callback_manager.on_tool_start -> _run -> on ToolException, `_handle_tool_error` renders handled content per handle_tool_error -> on_tool_end(output).

MCP adoption flow: MCPAdapter(target) -> str targets pass `_validate_url_target` -> FastMCPClient(target) -> `_arm_for_interrupts` (clones pre-built clients that lack an elicitation handler) -> `async with adapter` connects -> list_tools -> as_langchain_tool -> tools passed to create_agent.

CI unit-test flow: _test.yml -> uv_setup action -> `uv sync --group test --dev` -> `make test` (docker compose postgres+redis up, pytest -n auto --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket) -> get_min_versions.py -> `uv pip install $MIN_VERSIONS` -> `make tests` again -> git-clean check.

Release flow per AGENTS.md: bump `_version.py` + pyproject version + `uv lock`, merge `release(<partner>): <version>` PR, then `gh workflow run` on _release.yml — build -> release-notes -> pre-release-checks -> TestPyPI -> PyPI -> GitHub release/tag via ncipollo/release-action.

testing_signals.summary: pytest is the framework everywhere, configured per-package with strict markers/config, asyncio auto mode, syrupy snapshots, and pytest-socket to forbid network in unit tests. langchain_v1 has ~85 unit-test files (heavy agents/middleware coverage, plus chat_models, embeddings, mcp, tools), integration tests with VCR cassettes, and a benchmark suite for create_agent. CI runs tests twice — current and minimum dependency versions — and scheduled integration tests trace to LangSmith. langchain-tests packages the conformance suite partners must pass. Gaps: unit tests need docker postgres/redis for checkpointer paths, and langchain-classic's huge legacy surface relies on older coverage.

claims.claim: pytest config: `--strict-markers --strict-config --durations=5 --snapshot-warn-unused -vv`, asyncio_mode=auto, custom markers (requires, scheduled, compile, benchmark), syrupy snapshots under tests/**/__snapshots__.

Unit tests live in tests/unit_tests mirroring source layout; langchain_v1's agents suite includes test_react_agent.py, test_response_format*.py, test_return_direct*.py, test_subagent_*.py, middleware/ and middleware_typing/ dirs, plus specifications/ and cassettes/ for VCR replay.
Network isolation is enforced: `make test` runs pytest with `--disable-socket --allow-unix-socket` (pytest-socket), and unit tests must not hit the network per AGENTS.md.

Persistence tests are not hermetic: `make test`/`extended_tests`/`test_watch` spin up postgres and redis via `tests/unit_tests/agents/compose-postgres.yml` and `compose-redis.yml` before running, then tear them down.
Async correctness is checked with blockbuster (blocking-call detection) in the test group; freezegun and responses are used in core tests.
Benchmarks exist for agent creation: `make benchmark` runs tests/benchmarks/test_create_agent.py with -m benchmark; a codspeed workflow exists for perf tracking.
CI runs the unit suite twice — once on current deps and once after installing computed minimum versions via `.github/scripts/get_min_versions.py` — catching lower-bound regressions.

Scheduled integration tests (integration_tests.yml) trace runs to LangSmith using LANGSMITH_TRACING/API_KEY/PROJECT/TAGS env vars and authenticate to cloud providers via workload identity (google-github-actions/auth, configure-aws-credentials).

langchain-tests is a published package exposing standard unit+integration test classes (chat_models, embeddings, tools, vectorstores, retrievers, indexers, caches, sandboxes) that partner packages subclass for conformance.

Static checks are strict: ruff with `select = ["ALL"]` (google docstring convention, banned relative imports) and mypy strict mode with pydantic plugin; `check_imports` script verifies every module imports cleanly in CI.

Coverage is gated by make targets `coverage` and `coverage_agents` (term-missing + xml/html reports scoped to langchain.agents); test_react_agent.py is exempted from all lint rules, suggesting it is a large legacy-style test file.

risk_map.summary: The highest blast radius sits in places that execute or reach out: ShellToolMiddleware spawns real subprocesses (host/docker/codex policies), MCPAdapter intentionally blocks non-http(s) string targets because FastMCP would otherwise exec local files, and core's _security module provides SSRF validation with a test-only bypass env var. Fragile spots: regex-based model capability fallbacks that must track provider releases, a 9_999 recursion limit, deferred import errors from lazy provider loading, validation gaps when wrap_tool_call middleware exists, and the still-shipped langchain-classic legacy surface.

claims.claim: ShellToolMiddleware executes model-generated shell commands via subprocess.Popen (n noqa'd S603); HostExecutionPolicy runs commands directly on the host — DockerExecutionPolicy/CodexSandboxExecutionPolicy exist precisely because host execution is dangerous. Agents given this middleware have arbitrary-code-execution capability.

MCPAdapter._validate_url_target rejects any str target that is not http/https because fastmcp.Client tests strings as filesystem paths first and would launch a matching .py/.js file as a subprocess — a deliberate guard against config/model-supplied strings becoming local code execution.

core._security provides SSRF protection (validate_safe_url) blocking private IPs, localhost, cloud metadata, and k8s-internal addresses — but a `LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test` env var bypasses validation for hostnames starting with 'test' containing 'server', a foot-gun if set in production.

FALLBACK_MODELS_WITH_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT is a hand-maintained regex list of model names assumed to support provider-native structured output when profile data is missing — it will silently mispredict capabilities for new models until updated.

The compiled agent gets `recursion_limit: 9_999` (working around a langgraph issue), so a model stuck in a tool-call loop can iterate ~10k times before stopping — cost/runaway risk mitigated only by opt-in ModelCallLimitMiddleware/ToolCallLimitMiddleware.

Lazy provider loading means ImportError surfaces at first use, not import time: `_import_module` rewrites failures into 'pip install <pkg>' messages, and ollama has a langchain_community fallback that can mask which package is actually missing.

Client-side tool validation in `_get_bound_model` is skipped entirely when any middleware defines wrap_tool_call, so a typo'd dynamic tool name fails only when the middleware's own handler misses it — validation coverage depends on middleware correctness.

wrap_model_call middleware cannot return Command.goto (raises NotImplementedError pointing users at jump_to), and commands accumulate inner-first through the composed stack — ordering/return-shape mistakes produce runtime errors deep in the loop.

langchain-classic remains a large shipped legacy surface (chains/, agents/, retrievers/, utilities/ including many network-calling API wrappers); the dangerous LLMBashChain was removed — its module is now a stub raising AttributeError redirecting to langchain-experimental.

PIIMiddleware mutates streamed content in flight via _PIIStreamTransformer — silent redaction means downstream consumers (logs, users) see altered text; a false-positive detection corrupts model output with no record unless tracing is on.
Unit tests for persistence require live postgres/redis containers — a contributor running plain pytest without `make test`'s docker compose step will hit connection failures, not skips.

init_chat_model's 'langsmith' provider silently rewrites kwargs (openai_api_base -> gateway.smith.langchain.com, api key from LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY/LANGSMITH_API_KEY, use_responses_api=True) — credentials and traffic routing change based on env vars.

extension_points.summary: The framework is built around extension. Agents are extended via AgentMiddleware subclasses (six hook points + state_schema + transformers), custom tools (BaseTool/@tool/dict provider tools), custom state/context schemas, structured-output strategies, checkpointers/stores/caches from LangGraph, and stream transformers. Models and embeddings plug in through partner packages implementing core abstractions plus registry entries in _BUILTIN_PROVIDERS, validated by the langchain-tests conformance suite. Shell execution is extensible via BaseExecutionPolicy.

claims.claim: AgentMiddleware is the primary extension point: subclasses override any of before_agent/before_model/after_model/after_agent/wrap_model_call/wrap_tool_call (sync and/or async variants); decorators @before_agent/@before_model/@after_agent/@after_model/@dynamic_prompt/@wrap_model_call/@wrap_tool_call offer a functional alternative.

Middleware can declare `state_schema` (merged into agent state), `tools` (registered on the agent), `transformers` (stream post-processors), `trace_policy`, and `can_jump_to` per hook — factory.py inspects which hooks are overridden to decide which graph nodes to add.

New chat-model providers are added by implementing BaseChatModel in a partner package and adding a (module_path, class_name, creator_func) entry to `_BUILTIN_PROVIDERS`; custom creator lambdas handle non-standard constructors (e.g. huggingface's from_model_id, ibm's model_id kwarg).
New embeddings providers follow the identical registry pattern in embeddings/base.py `_BUILTIN_PROVIDERS`.
Partner packages prove conformance by subclassing langchain-tests suites (unit_tests/chat_models.py, integration_tests/vectorstores.py, etc.) rather than writing their own contract tests.
Tools plug in as BaseTool subclasses, @tool-decorated callables, or raw dicts (provider built-in tools); tools can inject runtime/state/store via ToolRuntime/InjectedState/InjectedStore annotations.

Agent state is extensible two ways: a custom `state_schema` TypedDict passed to create_agent (wins field conflicts over middleware schemas since it's merged last), or middleware-declared state_schema attributes.

Structured output strategies are pluggable ResponseFormat implementations (ToolStrategy, ProviderStrategy, AutoStrategy); callers can also pass raw Pydantic/dataclass/TypedDict/JSON-schema which get wrapped in AutoStrategy.

Persistence/streaming extension points come straight from LangGraph: create_agent accepts checkpointer (Checkpointer), store (BaseStore), cache (BaseCache), interrupt_before/after node names, and user `transformers` factories appended to the default pipeline.

Shell execution policy is pluggable via BaseExecutionPolicy subclasses — built-ins are HostExecutionPolicy, DockerExecutionPolicy, CodexSandboxExecutionPolicy, each implementing process launch and post-spawn limits.

Multi-agent composition is supported by naming an agent (`name=` becomes a subgraph node name) and by SubagentTransformer, which is always registered on the compiled graph to reshape nested-agent stream events.
Observability is extensible per-middleware via TracePolicy and process-wide via configure_trace_policy; all wrap_* hooks are traced through LangSmith `traceable` with scrubbed inputs.

agent_handoff.summary: Read AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md first — they encode the real conventions (uv-only, Conventional Commits with mandatory scope, Google docstrings, mypy strict + ruff ALL, no breaking signature changes). Work in libs/langchain_v1 for new features; libs/langchain (langchain-classic) is frozen. Re-export shims point at canonical homes: edit langchain_core or langgraph.prebuilt, not the shim. Tests must be hermetic unit tests under tests/unit_tests unless they need the docker services. Watch for: the manual structured-output model regexes, validation gaps around wrap_tool_call, and checkpointer tests that need containers.

claims.claim: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at repo root are the canonical contributor contract: uv for all env/dep ops (never pip/poetry), `uv sync --all-groups` before tests, make test/lint/format per package, Conventional Commits with mandatory scope, branch naming `<user>/<scope>/<desc>`.
New features go in libs/langchain_v1 (package `langchain`); libs/langchain ships `langchain-classic` and is explicitly 'legacy, no new features' per AGENTS.md — don't add capabilities there.

Public API stability is a hard rule: preserve signatures/positions/names, add new params keyword-only, mark experimental features with `!!! warning` docstring admonitions, and check `__init__.py` exports before touching anything public.

Several langchain_v1 modules are backwards-compat re-export shims — e.g. langchain/tools/tool_node.py re-exports langgraph.prebuilt ToolNode/ToolCallRequest, langchain/tools/__init__.py re-exports langchain_core.tools — so edit the canonical implementation, not the shim.

Before writing agent-loop code, read factory.py end-to-end: node names are '<middleware_name>.<hook>', edges must go through `_add_middleware_edge`/`_get_can_jump_to`, wrap handlers compose via `_chain_model_call_handlers`, and Command.goto inside wrap_model_call is unsupported.

Test conventions: mirror source layout under tests/unit_tests, no network (pytest-socket enforced), use fixtures/mocks, determinism required; persistence tests need `make start_services` (postgres+redis) first.

Lint bar is high: ruff `select = ["ALL"]` with google pydocstyle, single-backtick docstring code refs, banned relative imports, mypy strict with pydantic plugin and warn_unreachable; run `make lint` and `uv run --all-groups mypy .` before submitting.
Releasing a package = bump `_version.py` + pyproject version + `uv lock`, merge, then trigger _release.yml via `gh workflow run 63880841` — never tag or create GitHub releases manually.

Known traps: FALLBACK_MODELS_WITH_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT regexes must be updated for new model families; middleware-added tools bypass validation when wrap_tool_call exists; ModelRequest attribute mutation is deprecated (use override()); system_prompt param deprecated in favor of SystemMessage.

Model profile data (capabilities/context windows) is generated, not hand-edited: use `uv run langchain-profiles refresh --provider

--data-dir /langchain_

/data` from libs/model-profiles.

Every public module/function needs Google-style docstrings with Args/Returns/Raises, full type hints, and American English; tests get relaxed lint rules but still require the strict pytest config (no bare markers).

report.agent_prompt:
You are working in the LangChain Python monorepo (github.com/langchain-ai/langchain). It is a uv-managed collection of independently versioned packages under `libs/`.

## Layout
- `libs/core` -> `langchain-core` (v1.6.x): stable abstractions — `Runnable`, `BaseChatModel` (`language_models/chat_models.py`), `BaseTool` (`tools/base.py`), messages, callbacks, prompts, output parsers, vectorstores, `_security` (SSRF policy). Everything else builds on these.
- `libs/langchain_v1` -> `langchain` (v1.x): the actively maintained package. `create_agent()` in `langchain/agents/factory.py` compiles a LangGraph `StateGraph` implementing the model->tools loop with middleware hooks; `init_chat_model`/`init_embeddings` use `_BUILTIN_PROVIDERS` registries to lazily import partner packages; `langchain/agents/middleware/` holds the built-in middleware catalog (HITL, summarization, PII, retries, limits, shell tool, file search); `langchain/mcp/` adapts MCP servers (beta).
- `libs/langchain` -> `langchain-classic` (v1.0.x): frozen legacy chains/agents — no new features.
- `libs/partners/<name>`: provider integrations (openai, anthropic, ollama, ...), each independently released.
- `libs/standard-tests` -> `langchain-tests`: conformance suites partners subclass. `libs/model-profiles`: `langchain-profiles` CLI generating model capability data.

## Conventions (from AGENTS.md — read it fully)
- uv only for env/deps: `uv sync --all-groups`, `uv run --group test pytest ...`. Never pip/poetry/conda. Per-package `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` + Makefile.
- Commands: `make test` (needs docker for postgres/redis persistence tests), `make test_fast` (in-memory), `make lint` (ruff check+format --diff+mypy), `make format`.
- Quality bar: ruff `select=["ALL"]`, mypy strict, Google-style docstrings with Args/Returns/Raises, single backticks in docstrings, full type hints, keyword-only new params.
- Never break public signatures. Check `__init__.py` exports first. Deprecate via `langchain_core._api` decorators.
- PRs: Conventional Commits with mandatory scope (`feat(core):`, `fix(langchain):`, `release(openai): 0.2.6`); branches `<gh-user>/<scope>/<desc>`.

## Architecture essentials
`create_agent(model, tools, middleware=[...])`: resolves string models via `init_chat_model`, partitions middleware by overridden hooks, merges `state_schema`s (caller schema last = wins), adds `model`/`tools`/`<name>.<hook>` nodes, wires edges with `jump_to` support, and returns `graph.compile(checkpointer, store, ...).with_config(recursion_limit=9999)`. At runtime: START -> before_agent -> before_model -> model (through the composed `wrap_model_call` stack -> `_get_bound_model` -> `model.invoke` -> `_handle_model_output`) -> after_model -> conditional edge to `tools` or exit -> after_agent -> END. Structured output uses ToolStrategy/ProviderStrategy/AutoStrategy in `agents/structured_output.py`.

## Traps
- `langchain/tools/tool_node.py` and `tools/__init__.py` are re-export shims — canonical code lives in `langgraph.prebuilt` and `langchain_core.tools`.
- `FALLBACK_MODELS_WITH_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT` regexes in factory.py must be extended for new model families.
- ShellToolMiddleware runs real subprocesses; MCPAdapter rejects non-http(s) string targets because FastMCP would exec local files.
- `make check_imports` runs in CI — keep new modules importable without optional deps.
- Tests: mirror source layout under `tests/unit_tests`, no network (pytest-socket enforces), syrupy snapshots updated via `--snapshot-update` in `make test`.
